newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set new high, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set new high, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday set their sixth 33-month high this month after Wednesday's dip and analysts said the bull run fuelled by apparent foreign buying should continue, but at a slower pace.
"Yesterday we had a correction and now it seems we'll have stability or more growth," said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.

Analysts said gains by large-cap stocks such as industrial and trading firm Elektrim and computer maker Optimus suggested foreign institutions were still buying, perhaps because regional bourses seemed a better deal compared to some foreign exchanges.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.9 percent to 15,846.7 points and turnover eased 1.4 percent to 154.5 million zlotys ($53.2 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 54 to 13 with 18 stocks flat.

Elektrim and Optimus rose five percent and seven percent in active trade, while aluminium processor Kety and builder Mostostal Krakow rose 9.9 percent and 9.8 percent, with the latter extending its surge after starting trade on Tuesday.
Analysts said rubber producer Stomil Sanok, which started trade 120 percent above issue, should extend gains.

They said the central bank might wait for January's inflation data to decide whether to raise interest rates, as it has warned it might to curb fast credit growth. They said market expected Wednesday's 18.5-percent 1996 inflation figure.
Some analysts expected only a cosmetic rate change that would not dampen the market mood.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.9 percent to 157 zlotys ($54.1) and fell 2.9 perccent to 153 zlotys ($52.8) in continuous trade. Their turnover on the two markets was 30.6 million ($10.6 million) and 26 million zlotys ($9 million).
Live trade turnover was at 13 million zlotys ($4.5 million) with 13 stocks down, five up and three flat.
